definitions.explanation: A high-ranking military officer who commands a unit, base, or operation. Also used figuratively for leaders who direct large-scale operations.

examples.japanese: {司令官|しれいかん}が{命令|めいれい}を{出|だ}した。
{最高|さいこう}{司令官|しれいかん}として{作戦|さくせん}を{指揮|しき}する。
examples.english: To direct operations as supreme commander.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{司令官|しれいかん}が{着任|ちゃくにん}し、{部隊|ぶたい}の{士気|しき}が{高|たか}まった。
examples.english: The new commander took up his post, and the troops' morale rose.

notes:
Composed of {司令|しれい} (command, directing) + {官|かん} (officer, official). A formal military title for the officer in charge of a unit or base.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最高|さいこう}{司令官|しれいかん}: supreme commander
- {司令官|しれいかん}に{任命|にんめい}する: to appoint as commander
- {司令官|しれいかん}の{命令|めいれい}: the commander's order
- {総|そう}{司令官|しれいかん}: commander-in-chief

ETYMOLOGY:
{連合国軍最高司令官総司令部|れんごうこくぐんさいこうしれいかんそうしれいぶ} (GHQ/SCAP) was the headquarters of the Allied occupation of Japan after World War II, led by General MacArthur as {最高|さいこう}{司令官|しれいかん}.

RELATED WORDS:
- {司令部|しれいぶ}: headquarters, command center
- {指揮官|しきかん}: commanding officer — more general term for someone who directs
- {将軍|しょうぐん}: general — a military rank
